correctness.rationale: For any two embeddings, intersecting zero sets force disjoint one sets. Thus a common supersequence needs at least 2m copies of one letter. In a minimal word every pair of embeddings covers all positions, giving at most 2m of each. If both counts were 2m, the embeddings starting with the first m copies of their respective initial letters and continuing greedily would share the later of the two m-th positions, leaving an unused position. For a zero-rich word with m+j ones, split the ones into x,y,z around the m-th and (m+1)-st zero. Embeddability is y+z>=m and x+y>=m. When j>0, an empty flank would permit deletion of a one from the other flank or the center; with both flanks present, deleting a one on either side must violate the corresponding inequality, so both are tight. The j=0 case also forces tightness. Conversely, tightness makes every one essential, and deleting a zero violates the required 2m count. The separating zero positions make the factorization unique, and the two orientations are disjoint. The length and binomial-square formulas follow, including m=1; the backward ratios are at most 1/4 and tend to 1/4 at each fixed distance from the top, giving the 4/3 multiplier by geometric domination, then Stirling gives the total and longest-length fraction. Inspected frozen RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and check_minimal.cxx; the recorded exhaustive range m=1..5 is supplementary, not replayed or necessary for the proof.
